page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-8 is an ARM-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The instance is configured with 64 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with a PassMark memory score in the top 10% tier and uncached large-block read memory bandwidth reaching 200.21 GB/sec, which sits in the top 25%. Single-threaded compression and decompression tasks also perform in the top 25%, with gzip compression reaching 32.23 GB/sec. However, cryptographic performance is a notable bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25% at 1675.45, likely due to the lack of hardware-accelerated SHA extensions.

The instance delivers average multi-core CPU performance and standard database execution speeds, as evidenced by its 13062.53 score in PassMark database operations and 17.59 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. Medium-sized LLM inference prompt processing is relatively weak at 19.53 tokens per second. Given the high memory density and strong memory bandwidth, this instance is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, caching layers, and memory-bound data processing tasks that do not rely heavily on cryptographic acceleration or local disk storage.
